newsitem.title: UK: RJB to link with NatPower on new plant-paper.
newsitem.headline: RJB to link with NatPower on new plant-paper.

text.p: RJB Mining Plc is expected to announce a deal with electricity generator National Power on Monday on the development of RJB's planned "clean coal" power station in West Yorkshire, British newspapers said at the weekend.
Saturday's Financial Times and the Sunday Times said National Power was set to join RJB and Texaco Inc to develop Britain's first commercial clean coal-fired power station.
In February, RJB Mining said it was working with Texaco on a joint study to explore the feasibility of developing a 400 megawatt plant on a site adjacent to its Kellingley Colliery in West Yorkshire.

Yorkshire-based RJB, the successor of British Coal in England and Wales, said in February the station would consume about one million tonnes of coal a year -- half the planned output of the Kellingley mine, which employs 700 people.
It said the plant would take about two years to build once planning consents were secured.
RJB officials were not available for comment on Sunday, and a National Power spokesman declined to comment on the reports.
